source.title: Mixout: Effective Regularization to Finetune Large-scale Pretrained Language Models
source.authors: Cheolhyoung Lee; Kyunghyun Cho; Wan-Mo Kang

record.tranche_reason: The study compares dropout with mixout, a related regularization method, during BERT fine-tuning and reports held-out development and test scores; it does not test the claim versions about memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch size, sharpness, or removing memorized examples.
record.gate_note: The study's main intervention is mixout. Its dropout comparisons bear on V6, but it does not report a clear dropout-versus-no-dropout held-out result in text; Figure 4 and Figure 6 show the dropout sweeps.
record.test_reason: Section 4 varies dropout probability and measures held-out MNIST accuracy in a pretrained 784–300–100–10 fully connected classifier, bearing on V6 in a transfer-learning setting. The BERT experiments concern transformers and do not directly test V6's fully connected or convolutional classifier claim.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that mixout regularizes toward pretrained parameters with an adaptive strength, improves BERT fine-tuning stability on small downstream datasets, and improves average and best performance across runs. These are aggregate conclusions, not improvements for every configuration or metric; the larger SST-2 dataset shows similar performance between recipes.
record.recipe_differences: Compares mixout and dropout while fine-tuning pretrained BERT and a fully connected network; it does not reproduce the original dropout study's image-classification experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with mix probability, task, and whether regularization is applied to the additional output layer. Mixout incurs about 32.5% more training time than dropout in the reported RTE experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: In BERT fine-tuning without weight decay, Appendix F reports the highest mean development scores at dropout probability 0.1 for MRPC and STS-B, but at zero dropout for RTE and CoLA. Exact differences are not recoverable from the supplied figure text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dropout's benefit during pretrained-transformer fine-tuning depends on the downstream task and dropout probability.

fits_no_version.finding: With pretrained BERT layers held at mixout probability 0.7, adding output-layer dropout at probability 0.7 lowers mean development scores on all four tasks; MRPC's maximum rises from 91.1 to 92.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output-layer dropout during transformer fine-tuning can reduce average performance while improving the best run on some tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixout improves fine-tuning stability and average development performance relative to the tested dropout-based recipe on small GLUE datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Regularizing toward pretrained parameters can improve transformer fine-tuning compared with the tested dropout and weight-decay recipe.

record.problems: The dropout probability sweeps are shown in figures without recoverable exact values in the supplied text. The main comparisons concern mixout versus dropout and do not isolate dropout against an unregularized baseline in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the dropout sweep results are figure-only in the supplied text, and the reported numerical tables compare dropout combined with weight decay against mixout configurations rather than isolating dropout's effect.

untested.parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets.

The supplied text does not establish dropout's accuracy benefit over no dropout in the fully connected MNIST experiment. Very small image-training sets, training-loss evidence of underfitting, convolutional classifiers, and removing dropout and weight decay with augmentation are not tested.
Removing examples selected by label memorization.

missing.what: The fully connected image-classifier dropout sweep is omitted. Figure 2(b) reports mean MNIST validation accuracy and standard deviation across ten restarts as dropout probability varies. The text identifies high accuracy at probabilities 0.1–0.3 and greater probability sensitivity than mixout, but does not supply exact dropout values or an explicit no-dropout comparison. Recover the plotted values and baseline before assigning a directional V6 verdict. This experiment is not declared in rows_left_out.

record.verdict_notes: No extracted rows exist to correct. The record overlooks the fully connected MNIST experiment relevant to V6. No V6 verdict is assigned because the supplied prose does not establish the direction of dropout's effect relative to an appropriate baseline. BERT dropout results cannot establish that effect for the architecture classes specified in V6.

The study varies dropout probability during BERT fine-tuning, but the dropout-versus-no-dropout values are only shown in figures and the text does not state a clear held-out effect. It does not test the specified fully connected or convolutional image-classifier settings, small training-set boundary, or data-augmentation comparison.
